agentOverflow.title: Agent Overflow Allocation
agentOverflow.tooltip: Configure how free agents are distributed once every job at every priority tier has filled to its max_agents cap.
agentOverflow.priorityFifoDescription: Tiers fill highest-priority first. Once a tier hits max_agents, remaining agents pile on the OLDEST job in that tier — exceeding its cap. Lower-priority jobs may starve until higher tiers are exhausted.
agentOverflow.priorityRoundRobinDescription: Tiers fill highest-priority first. Once a tier hits max_agents, remaining agents rotate evenly across that tier's jobs — exceeding caps. Lower-priority jobs may starve.
agentOverflow.enforceMaxAgentsDescription: Strictly cap each job at its max_agents limit — no overflow. Surplus agents stay idle. Most predictable; can waste capacity.
agentOverflow.maxAgentsFifoDescription: All jobs at all priorities fill to max_agents first (strict caps). Any remaining agents then pile on the OLDEST job overall — bypassing priority. Maximizes throughput while still giving every job its baseline.
agentOverflow.maxAgentsRoundRobinDescription: All jobs at all priorities fill to max_agents first (strict caps). Any remaining agents then rotate evenly across ALL jobs — bypassing priority. Maximizes throughput with fair distribution beyond the baseline.

potfile.description: The potfile collects cracked passwords from all jobs and reuses them in subsequent attacks. Higher batch sizes process more passwords at once but take longer per cycle.

speedTest.title: Speed Test (Benchmark)
speedTest.tooltip: Tune how long agents wait for hashcat to produce a usable benchmark before failing the speed test. Compressed wordlists need significantly more time to dictstat-preprocess.
speedTest.timeoutUncompressedHelper: Maximum seconds the agent will wait for a valid speed reading on plain-text wordlists. Default: 120.
speedTest.timeoutCompressedHelper: Maximum seconds for .gz / .zip / .xz wordlists — the three formats hashcat reads natively. These need longer to decompress and dictstat-preprocess. Default: 300.
speedTest.minStatusUpdatesHelper: Minimum number of hashcat --status-json ticks the agent must collect before returning a result. Default: 3.
speedTest.minUpdatesLowWarning: Values below 3 may produce inaccurate readings: GPUs may not have finished spinning up.
speedTest.description: If the agent times out without producing a non-zero speed, the benchmark is reported as failed and the job surfaces an admin-actionable error. The chunking pipeline also refuses to dispatch a 1-candidate task, so a stale 0 H/s benchmark cannot loop forever.

intro.title: Cloud GPU provisioning
intro.body: Rent GPU instances on demand when the on-prem fleet cannot keep up. Instances join your existing VPN, receive only the files their job needs, and are torn down automatically. Spend is committed against a per-client budget before an instance boots, so a cap is a real limit rather than an after-the-fact measurement.

providers.title: Cloud providers
providers.description: Where rented instances come from, and how they reach this server.
providers.deleteBody: Delete "{{name}}"? This fails while any rented instance still references it.
providers.empty: No cloud providers configured. Nothing will be rented.
providers.preflightFailedBody: This provider cannot launch instances yet.

preflightSections.inconclusive: Could not be verified (treated as failure)

ackBody.vastai: Vast.ai rents GPUs on individually-owned machines whose operators have root access to the container. Hashes, wordlists and cracked plaintexts placed there are visible to a third party. This is categorically different from AWS or RunPod Secure Cloud, where instances run inside your own account or in SOC 2 datacenters.
ackBody.runpod_community: RunPod Community Cloud rents GPUs on peer-operated machines whose owners have root access to the container. Hashes, wordlists and cracked plaintexts placed there are visible to a third party. RunPod’s compliance attestations cover Secure Cloud only and do not extend to this tier.

providers.ackConfirm: Do you accept this exposure for workloads sent to this provider?
providers.ephemeralKeyBody: KH_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set, so a random key was generated at startup. Every stored credential becomes unreadable after the next restart. Set KH_ENCRYPTION_KEY before saving provider credentials.
providers.vpnSectionHelp: This server is never exposed to the internet, so rented instances join the VPN you already run. OpenVPN is not supported: it needs /dev/net/tun and CAP_NET_ADMIN, which Vast.ai's unprivileged containers do not provide.
providers.reusableKeyWarning: A reusable key is shared by every instance and expires (Tailscale caps auth keys at 90 days). Once it lapses, provisioning is refused rather than launching instances that cannot connect. An OAuth client or PAT lets KrakenHashes mint a single-use ephemeral key per instance instead.
providers.staticConfigWarning: WireGuard uses a static peer config: there is no per-instance credential and no automatic deregistration when an instance dies. Tailscale or NetBird is safer.

credentialKinds.oauth: OAuth client — mint one ephemeral key per instance (recommended)
credentialKinds.pat: Access token — mint one ephemeral key per instance (recommended)
credentialKinds.reusable_key: Reusable key — shared by every instance, expires

vpnCredentialHelp.oauth: Tailscale OAuth client as client_id:client_secret. Needs the auth_keys scope and the tag selected.
vpnCredentialHelp.pat: NetBird personal access token or service-user token.
vpnCredentialHelp.reusable_key: The pre-authorized key every instance will use.

RunPod's SOC 2, ISO 27001 and PCI DSS attestations cover Secure Cloud only, not this tier. Enable it only for clients whose data may be exposed to a third party, and acknowledge it per client as well.

rules.title: When the system may spend
rules.description: Budgets govern how much may be spent. These govern when anything may be spent at all. Without them the autoscaler rents after a single starving tick, for any job, at any hour, with no per-job ceiling.
rules.inheritBody: Clients inherit each field individually, so tightening a default here reaches every client that has not overridden that specific field. Per-client overrides are edited on the client screen.

fields.windowEnabled: Restrict provisioning to a time window

helperText.minJobPriority: Absolute priority, not a percentage. Your current ceiling is {{ceiling}}.
helperText.floorOff: No floor: any cloud-burst job qualifies for automatic provisioning.
helperText.minStarvation: How long a job must make no progress at all before paid capacity is rented. 0 rents on the first starving tick. Applies to the autoscaler only.
helperText.skipIfFinishing: Do not rent for a job projected to finish this soon on existing capacity — a rented instance needs 5-10 minutes to boot and sync. 0 never skips.
helperText.maxSpendPerJob: Whole-life cap on cloud spend for one job, not month-windowed. Blank means no cap. Enforced everywhere, including manual admin provisioning.
helperText.windowEnabled: Governs starts only. Instances are never torn down because the window closed — TTL and idle drain own teardown.
helperText.windowTz: IANA name, e.g. America/Chicago. Leave blank for UTC.
helperText.windowWrap: A closing time earlier than the opening time wraps midnight, which is the normal way to write "only rent overnight". Setting both to the same value means always open.
